findings.note: Shipped `fsm diff` JSON carries a dead field whose doc comment asserts a property it does not have, and the spec's CallRow contract does not declare it. machine.CallRow.Index (internal/fsm/machine/diff.go:29-33) is exported with `json:"index"` and documented as "Index distinguishes several calls of one kind in the same node@iter with the same input - the same question put to two models. Without it the rows collided and the earlier call vanished from the report." It is never assigned anywhere in the package (the only `.Index` writes are CallSide.Index at diff.go:109 and machine.go:1066); the real disambiguator is the unexported `occurrence` field (diff.go:38, 101-105, 141). So every row of the report serialises `"index":0`, and the report is emitted verbatim to the CLI envelope at internal/fsm/cli/run.go:918, i.e. a consumer that reads the documented field to group repeated calls gets a constant. The spec's own CallRow declaration (docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-fork.md:164) lists no Index on CallRow, and the ledger row at line 342 records only a "per-side Index", so spec and code disagree about the output contract. Either set the field from `occurrence` (and add it to the spec's CallRow) or delete it.

evidence.note: spec CallRow has no Index field; ledger line 342 records only per-side Index
exported json:"index" field, documented as the repeat disambiguator, never assigned; occurrence at line 38 does the work
the Report is shipped as-is in the fsm diff envelope, so "index":0 reaches consumers

findings.note: The spec's r5 change header names a torn-tail file the code never writes, and contradicts the same document's own body. Line 24 says the torn tail is "preserved to `runs.jsonl.torn-<ts>`"; section 6 at line 251 says `.metareview/runs/.torn/runs.jsonl-<unixnano>`, the F9 test row at line 317 says `runs/.torn/runs.jsonl-*`, and internal/fsm/record/record.go:219-223 actually writes filepath.Join(root, ".metareview", "runs", ".torn", fmt.Sprintf("runs.jsonl-%d", nanos())). The header is the part an operator reads when recovering a torn append, so it points at a filename that will never exist.

findings.note: Manifest.Bytes is specified as one thing and implemented as another, and MaxBytes is enforced against the smaller number. The spec (line 189) declares `Bytes int64 /* sum of all written files */` and section 5 states the bundle "is built in memory and MaxBytes is checked before the first write". In internal/fsm/export/export.go the field's own comment (line 80) says "every written file except manifest.json itself", and the accumulation loop at lines 167-169 runs before `files["manifest.json"]` is inserted at line 173. So (a) the documented meaning of a manifest field is wrong, and (b) an export whose payload sits just under MaxBytes writes more than MaxBytes bytes to disk - the cap systematically undercounts by the manifest's own size. Pick one meaning and make the spec, the field comment and the MaxBytes check agree.

evidence.note: spec Manifest: Bytes = sum of all written files
m.Bytes accumulated over files before manifest.json is added at line 173; MaxBytes compared at line 170

findings.note: The new test file's headline test covers a wrapper with no production caller, so it gives assurance about a path that never runs. ctxDeps.applyJudgeOverride (internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:250-256, a file added whole by this PR) is called only from internal/fsm/cli/judgeoverride_test.go:45, 57 and 63; the shipped path is applyJudgeOverrideFor, invoked once at internal/fsm/cli/run.go:307 with the calibration bool. Grepping the whole tree for `applyJudgeOverride(` returns exactly those three test call sites plus the definition. Because tests/coverage.sh gates every internal/fsm/* package at exactly 100.0% of statements (tests/coverage.sh header, lines 10-12), this dead wrapper is kept green solely by the test written for it - the failure mode that gate exists to prevent. Either delete the wrapper and retarget TestApplyJudgeOverrideCopiesAndOverlays at applyJudgeOverrideFor(..., false), or give it a real caller.

evidence.note: the only callers of applyJudgeOverride are this test's lines 45, 57 and 63
applyJudgeOverride delegates to applyJudgeOverrideFor(..., false) and has no non-test caller
the production path calls applyJudgeOverrideFor directly with p.bools["calibration"]

findings.note: Both change-header lines describing CommonPrefixSeq are stale and mutually inconsistent with section 4 and with the code. Line 22 (r4) says the comparison is over `(Type, Node, Data)` - omitting At, which is precisely the field that stops a child's fresh `tree` from extending the prefix. Line 30 (r5) says the "tuple includes `Origin` presence". Section 4 (line 174 onward) says `(Type, Node, At, Data)` with Origin, Seq and Prev ignored, and commonPrefix in internal/fsm/machine/diff.go:186-196 implements exactly section 4. The body is right; the two header claims are wrong.
